_comment: tests/benchmark/hook_latency.py on held-out task 0cb3760383's hermes-agent index (built by v4.22.1; an APFS clone) and prompt (bench/task_outcome/hermes-agent-test-ranking/heldout/tasks.json), on an M3 with macOS's mediaanalysisd using ~1.3 cores throughout (load averages in each run). Each NeuralMind ran from a copy on PYTHONPATH: 'before' is main at 923068b1 (4.23.1); 'after' is this change; an 'upgraded' copy is the same code with __version__ set to 4.99.0. An upgrade is simulated by running the upgraded copy with --states cached on the cache the previous step left, so its first sample is the first prompt after the upgrade. Steps ran in this order, on one index: before_all_states; before_upgraded (cache written by 4.23.1); after_all_states; after_upgraded (cache written by this change); before_reads_after_cache (4.23.1 on that cache: a miss, which rewrites it with its own header); after_upgraded_from_4_23_1 (this change, upgraded, on the cache 4.23.1 wrote); before_upgraded_again. Reproduce a step: python -m tests.benchmark.hook_latency <index> --tasks bench/task_outcome/hermes-agent-test-ranking/heldout/tasks.json --task 0cb3760383 --label hermes-agent-0cb3760383 --runs 5 [--states cached]

before_all_states.prompt: My session is running on Anthropic (`https://api.anthropic.com` with my Anthropic key). My config has no `model.base_url`, but `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is set in my environment. When I switch the session's model with provider `custom` (e.g. `/model m2 --provider custom`, or when the per-turn config sync picks up `provider: custom`), the switch succeeds but the session now points at OpenRouter's default endpoint with my OpenRouter key, a host I never chose. When a custom endpoint is configured in `model.base_url`, switching to `custom` from another provider correctly uses that endpoint. But when no custom endpoint is configured, the switch should keep the session's current endpoint and API key (here `https://api.anthropic.com` and my Anthropic key) instead of falling through to OpenRouter.
